references.text: The Spirit of the Lord began to stir Samson in Mahaneh-Dan, between Zorah and Eshtaol—the same places where he was later buried.
Samson went down to Ashkelon, showing his connection to the family and relatives who later came to retrieve his body.
It is mentioned here that Samson judged Israel for twenty years during the time of the Philistines, a period confirmed in this verse.
Zorah is noted as the hometown of Manoah, Samson's father, and it is where Samson was buried in his father's tomb.
Joshua was also buried in his family's inheritance, a similar pattern where a leader in Israel is laid to rest in the family burial place.
Jacob asked to be buried with his fathers, reflecting the same tradition of family burials we see here with Samson.
Samson is mentioned among the heroes of faith who by faith performed acts of righteousness and obtained what was promised.
